summary: The main article describes a transition-metal-free photocatalytic synthesis of acylsulfonamides using 4CzBN as a photocatalyst. It includes an optimization table for reaction conditions, a substrate scope table covering various hydroxamic acids and sulfinates, and three schemes detailing synthetic methods, control experiments, and the proposed reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Methods for Preparing Acylsulfonamides
items.description: Compares traditional acylation methods and multicomponent reactions with the newly developed photocatalytic S-N coupling approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization Study a
items.description: Summarizes the screening of photocatalysts, reductants, and phase-transfer catalysts to optimize the yield of the acylsulfonamide product.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate Scope of the Reaction a
items.description: Displays the variety of hydroxamic acids and sodium organosulfinates compatible with the optimized reaction conditions.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Control Experiments
items.description: Details experiments involving radical traps, atmosphere control, and intermediate identification to probe the reaction pathway.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Mechanistic Studies: (a) Fluorescence Spectra of 4CzBN with Various Concentrations of 2a; (b) UV-Visible Spectra of ABDA with 4CzBN with Various Irradiation Time; (c) Time Trace Analysis of 3a and 3a ′ Formation under Different Conditions; and (d) Plausible Mechanism
items.description: Combines spectroscopic data and time trace analysis to propose a mechanism involving singlet oxygen and nitrosocarbonyl intermediates.
